pages.observed: Five phone samples 0.0 s to 0.8 s of option A. Airport curb scene with a phone ride-request card at upper left, an airplane/car pickup sign at right, and a white roof-sensor SUV sliding in from the left toward a chevron-marked pickup bay. Caption box in lower middle from 0.2 s.

Option A 1.0 s to 1.8 s. The white roof-sensor SUV is now stopped inside the white pickup bay outline at mid frame, with a red glow at its rear brake lamp. Phone card at upper left still reads Ride requested. Frames 1.2 to 1.8 s appear identical.

Option A 2.0 to 2.8 s. Exterior car holds at the bay while a small blank Texas outline card appears at top right. At 2.6 s the shot cuts to the cabin seen from behind the front seats: steering wheel at left, dash screen with a route, empty seats, airplane pickup sign through the windshield. The ride-requested phone card stays at upper left over the cabin view.

Option A 3.0 to 3.8 s, interior view. The steering wheel rim marker moves clockwise with no hands on the wheel, the airport sign drifts right out of the windshield as the car moves, and the dash screen route dot advances. A Texas outline locator draws at top right. Seats are empty. Phone card overlay and caption remain.

Option A 4.0 to 4.8 s. The cabin view holds with almost no change: wheel marker resting at right, windshield mostly an empty pale field with only a sliver of the blue sign at right, empty seats, dash route screen. Phone card and caption unchanged.

Option A 5.0 to 5.8 s. Cabin view holds to 5.2 s, then cuts to a curb close: a large tilted phone with a route map stands in the left foreground and the white roof-pod car sits at the bay behind it beside the airplane sign. The phone still says Ride requested through 5.8 s. Caption the airport included. The Texas locator rings a county at 5.8 s.

Option A 6.0 to 6.8 s. The phone car icon travels to the pin and the screen changes from Ride requested to Arriving, At the curb, while the white roof-pod car holds at the bay beside the airplane sign. The caption the airport included shows to 6.4 s and then clears.

Option A 7.0 to 7.8 s. A pale paper map lies on a brown plank table in the open, with a small February calendar page standing at its top right corner and a few tiny car pins near center. The map is nearly blank until 7.8 s, when a short blue river stroke and a thin line start drawing. Caption The service began in February from 7.2 s.

Option A 8.0 to 8.8 s. On the paper map, a blue river line draws from top to bottom, a second thin blue line appears at right, and gray street lines and a faint ring road draw across the grid around the small car pins. The Texas locator card fades away. The February page sits still at the map corner.

Option A 9.0 to 9.8 s. After the medium map hold, the shot moves closer on the map. A pinned tag reading 60 square miles, Limited area swings onto the top of the map and the February page slides in and lands tilted at lower right. At 9.8 s only a short dark outline stroke has started; no closed outline yet. Caption in a limited area of sixty square miles.

Option A 10.0 to 10.8 s. On the closer map a black outline line keeps tracing clockwise from the upper left, across the top under the 60 square miles tag and down the right side toward the car pins. The February page shifts to the lower left corner. The outline is still open at 10.8 s.

Option A 11.0 to 11.8 s. The black outline finishes tracing and closes into a shaded polygon around the three car pins and across the river, under the 60 square miles, Limited area tag, with the February page at lower left. The completed shape holds through 11.8 s.

Option A 12.0 to 12.8 s. The completed shaded service outline holds on the map with the three car pins moving slightly inside it, the 60 square miles tag above and the February page at lower left. The caption is gone at 12.8 s.

Option A 13.0 to 13.8 s. Last map frame, then a cut to a wide brown creek under pale sky with flat-topped trees on the far bank and pale stepped limestone ledges at right. A small white roof-pod car sits in the water up to its lower doors with its reflection below. Faint rain streaks. Disclosure now reads Illustration. A different car, April 20th account.

Option A 14.0 to 14.8 s. The small white roof-pod car stays in the brown creek with its reflection; the frame drifts slightly and rain streaks continue. From 14.6 s a pale splash line shows at the car's right side and the car tilts a little. The car is small, roughly one sixth of frame width.

Option A 15.0 to 15.8 s. The white roof-pod car sits in the brown creek with a pale wake trailing from its front right. At about 15.4 s the framing moves closer; through 15.8 s the car tilts with its nose rising and front wheel lifting out of the water while drifting slightly. Dark seat-back shapes show in the windows.

Option A 16.0 to 16.8 s. The white roof-pod car, tilted nose up with a tan mud band on its lower body, stays near the same place in frame while the far-bank trees slide left, so the car is traveling to the right with a pale bow wave curling ahead of its front wheel. The car faces and moves in its own forward direction rather than sideways.

Option A 17.0 to 17.8 s. The creek car keeps moving right with its bow wave until about 17.4 s. At 17.6 s the film cuts to a wide flooded street: brown water across the road in front of low tan houses with a live oak and green street signs, a small white roof-pod car standing in the water, and a pale sidewalk in the lower third. Disclosure reads Illustration. Another car, earlier in April.

Option A 18.0 to 18.8 s. The small white roof-pod car rolls slowly right on the flooded residential street while the brown water climbs from its wheels to over the lower wheel arches. Low tan houses, a live oak and green street signs stand behind. The caption sits just under the car over the lower water band.

Option A 19.0 to 19.8 s. The small white roof-pod car is stopped in brown water above its wheel arches on the residential street. At 19.6 to 19.8 s tiny amber glows appear at its front and rear corners. The car occupies roughly a third of frame width; the amber lamps are a few pixels across.

Option A 20.0 to 20.8 s. Closer side view of the white roof-pod car stopped in brown floodwater up to its wheel arches, houses and a live oak softened behind. Amber lamps at both ends glow, dim and glow again across the samples. Dark seat-back shapes show through the side windows; no person is visible.

Option A 21.0 to 21.8 s. The closer side view of the stopped white car in floodwater holds, with amber lamps blinking at both ends and the water level steady at the wheel arches. The frame drifts slightly. Caption unchanged.

Option A 22.0 to 22.8 s. After a last frame of the stopped flood car, the film cuts to a flat olive wall over a brown desk band. A cream card headed Federal recall record, Vehicle safety recall slides in from the right and settles tilted, with a dark pen at its right edge and its right side cropped by the frame. At 22.8 s field text starts typing: Reca and Sof.

Option A 23.0 to 23.8 s. The cream record card settles near center on the brown desk and its rows type in: Recall type, Software, then Potential units affected, 3,791. A dark pen lies still at the card's lower right. Caption Waymo filed a software recall.

Option A 24.0 to 24.8 s. The finished record card holds on the desk. At about 24.6 s the framing changes: the card moves to the top of frame just below the disclosure label, a wooden stamp handle edge appears at right, and a grid of faint empty car outlines fills the lower desk. At 24.8 s the first three white car icons fill in. Caption that could affect nearly thirty eight hundred cars.

Option A 25.0 to 25.8 s. Below the record card a ten-wide grid of small white car icons fills row by row until about five rows are full. A hand in a blue sleeve enters from the right holding a wooden stamp and moves it over the upper part of the card by 25.8 s. The card's top edge sits just below the disclosure label.

Option A 26.0 to 26.8 s. A hand in a blue sleeve holds a wooden stamp pressed over the record card header while the five-row car icon grid stays full below. A tag reading Nearly 3,800 vehicles, 3,791 potentially affected in the record swings in and settles between card and grid. At 26.8 s an amber stamp outline starting So shows on the card, mostly still covered by the stamp block and hand.

Option A 27.0 to 27.8 s. The hand pulls the stamp away to the right, leaving an amber Software recall stamp mark on the card's upper right. The counter tag and the full car icon grid hold below. Completed record composition holds through 27.8 s.

Option A 28.0 to 28.8 s. After the finished record composition, the film cuts to a wide side view of a road with lane lines, a grass verge, a street lamp, trees and a distant skyline. The white roof-pod car enters from the left. At 28.8 s a pale quote card fades in near the top with the recall sentence. No standing water is drawn on the road yet.

Option A 29.0 to 29.8 s. The camera tracks the white roof-pod car traveling right along the road; lane dashes and background slide past. The quote card with the full recall sentence sits at top. The caption box sits just below the car, covering the road edge. No standing water is visible yet.

Option A 30.0 to 30.8 s. The tracked white car continues right; from 30.6 s its rear brake lamp glows red and the background scroll slows. At 30.8 s the edge of a pale gray-blue water patch appears at the right edge of the road. The quote card holds at top and the caption under the car.

Option A 31.0 to 31.8 s. The white car creeps right with its red brake lamp lit (to 31.4 s) toward a pale gray-blue elongated water patch at the right side of the road. The car stays a short distance from the water. The caption box overlaps the lower part of the water patch and the road edge.

Option A 32.0 to 32.8 s. In the wide view the car keeps creeping toward the pale water patch but has not reached it when the caption clears at 32.6 s. At 32.8 s the film cuts to a close side view of the car, now large, on gray road with the quote card above; a thin pale wavy line runs along the road at the tires but no water body is visible yet.

Option A 33.0 to 33.8 s. Close side view of the large white car on the road with headlamp beam ahead. A pale gray-blue water patch slides in from the right edge toward the front wheel but has not reached it by 33.8 s. The quote card above shows the full recall sentence with no highlighted word.

Option A 34.0 to 34.8 s. The large white car's front wheel meets the pale standing water at 34.0 s and the water spreads under the front of the car with ripple marks at the tire by 34.8 s. At 34.2 s an amber highlight box lands on the word may in the quote card's first line and holds.

Option A 35.0 to 35.8 s. The large white car is in the pale standing water across its full length, with diagonal wake lines trailing behind both wheels and spray at the front tire. The quote card keeps the amber highlight on may. The caption box covers the lower part of the wake.

Option A 36.0 to 36.8 s. The white car keeps rolling through the pale standing water, wake lines streaming from its wheels, as the background tree slides left. The may highlight holds. After the caption clears at 36.6 s the whole water patch and wake are visible beneath the car.

Option A 37.0 to 37.8 s. Cut to the federal recall record card, now taller, on the brown desk. A Remedy row opens below the earlier fields and types The remedy is currently under development; by 37.6 s the row is complete and lit with a warm peach tint. Caption reads the same sentence.

Option A 38.0 to 38.8 s. With the remedy row lit, a hand in a blue sleeve brings a pen in from the right; by 38.6 s the pen tip rests on the remedy row beside the word currently. The rest of the card is unchanged.

Option A 39.0 to 39.8 s. The pen hand keeps its tip on the remedy row while a second blue-sleeved arm enters from the lower right holding a wooden stamp and lowers it over the lower part of the remedy panel. Two forearms, both from the right edge, are on the card at once. The framing tightens slightly at 39.2 s.

Option A 40.0 to 40.8 s. The second hand presses the wooden stamp on the lower remedy panel, then lifts and slides it right, revealing an amber Under development stamp mark beneath the remedy text by 40.6 s. The pen hand stays resting on the row.

Option A 41.0 to 41.8 s. Both hands withdraw from the finished record card, leaving the Under development stamp. At 41.6 s the film cuts to a lot with four white roof-pod cars in angled bays under a wire strung between two poles, an April calendar page at left and a Vehicle maps card at right. At 41.8 s a weather limits tag swings in from the left edge, still partly off frame.

Option A 42.0 to 42.8 s. A tag reading Weather limits, tightened, with a cloud and rain icon, slides along the overhead wire from the left edge and pins near center above the row of four parked white cars. April page at left and Vehicle maps card at right hold. Caption As an interim step, Waymo tightened its weather limits.

Option A 43.0 to 43.8 s. The weather limits tag drifts slowly right along the wire above the four parked cars and tilts slightly at 43.8 s. Everything else in the lot holds still under the same caption.

Option A 44.0 to 44.8 s. The lot composition holds with only a slight rocking of the weather limits tag on the wire. The four cars, the April page and the maps card are unchanged; no check marks and no date change yet.

Option A 45.0 to 45.8 s. The lot holds; the caption clears at 45.4 s, the framing pushes in slightly at 45.6 s, and the next caption appears at 45.8 s. The cars carry no check marks yet and the calendar page still shows only April.

Option A 46.0 to 46.8 s. Round white check-mark badges appear above the parked cars one by one from left to right, three complete by 46.6 s and the fourth drawing at 46.8 s. The calendar page still shows only April.

Option A 47.0 to 47.8 s. All four parked cars now carry check-mark badges. A small check mark draws onto the Vehicle maps card with a tiny label under it. The calendar page still reads only April through 47.8 s.

Option A 48.0 to 48.8 s. The lot with all four checked cars and the checked maps card holds; at 48.8 s the calendar page flips to show a large 20 beneath the April header, after the four cars were already checked.

Option A 49.0 to 49.8 s. The calendar page settles on April 20 as the turned sheet lifts away above it. The four checked cars, the checked Vehicle maps card and the weather limits tag hold. Caption clears at 49.8 s.

Option A 50.0 to 50.8 s. Cut back to the same airport curb composition as the opening: the white roof-pod car sits in the pickup bay beside the airplane sign, with the phone card at upper left now reading Arriving. Disclosure reads Illustration. A generic airport ride, not the flood cars. No door opening yet in these samples.

Option A 51.0 to 51.8 s. At the airport bay the white car's rear side door opens from 51.2 s, revealing a dark interior and a pale seat, and stays open through 51.8 s. The door is small at phone size, about a sixth of frame width. Phone card reads Arriving.

Option A 52.0 to 52.8 s. The open-door car holds at the bay until the caption clears at 52.6 s. At 52.8 s a new medium framing shows the curb, bench, suitcase and sign with the open-door car, a small phone propped at the curb, and a small federal recall record card lying flat on the asphalt in the foreground with its remedy row and Under development stamp.

Option A 53.0 to 53.8 s. The open-door car holds at the bay while the small record card, reading The remedy is currently under development with an Under development stamp, floats on the asphalt between the car and the caption, drifting and tilting slightly. Card text is small at phone size; its stamp text is not legible.

Option A 54.0 to 54.8 s. The record card grows and slides toward the lower left foreground until it is large and readable, with its Remedy row The remedy is currently under development and an Under development stamp. Its bottom edge meets the caption box and its top edge reaches the car's wheel line; the open-door car stays at the bay above it.

Option A 55.0 to 55.8 s. The composition holds: the open-door white car at the bay above and the large record card at lower left with its remedy row and Under development stamp, the card's top edge touching the car's front wheel. Caption below. Only slight drift.

Option A 56.0 to 56.8 s. After a brief caption gap, the film cuts at 56.4 s to a split frame: the upper band shows the white car at the airport bay with its rear door open, larger than before, and the lower band shows the record card with Under development beside a small phone on a brown desk. Caption as currently under development.

Option A 57.0 to 57.8 s. The split holds: open-door car at the airport bay above, record card and phone on the desk below. A dark underline draws under the words under development on the card and extends across the line by 57.8 s. Caption as currently under development.

Option A 58.0 to 58.8 s. The final split of the open-door airport car above and the underlined Under development record card below holds until about 58.4 s, then cuts at 58.6 s to a dark credits card with a Texas flag icon, Texas AI Docket wordmark, texasaidocket.com and the sources, illustration, map and music credits.
Option A 59.0 to 59.8 s. The dark credits card holds unchanged: Texas flag icon, Texas AI Docket wordmark, texasaidocket.com, sources, illustration, map and music credits.
Option A 60.0 to 60.8 s. The same dark credits card holds unchanged with the Texas flag icon, Texas AI Docket wordmark, URL and credit lines.
Option A 61.0 to 61.8 s. The dark credits card holds unchanged with the Texas flag icon, Texas AI Docket wordmark, URL and credit lines.
Option A 62.0 to 62.8 s. The dark credits card continues to hold unchanged with the Texas flag icon, Texas AI Docket wordmark, URL and credit lines.
Option A 63.0 to 63.433 s, final four samples including the last phone frame 1903. The dark credits card holds unchanged to the end of the film.

Option B 0.0 to 0.8 s. Same airport curb opening as option A: phone card reading Ride requested at upper left, airplane pickup sign at right, and the white roof-pod car sliding in from the left toward the chevron pickup bay. Caption from 0.2 s.
Option B 1.0 to 1.8 s. The white roof-pod car sits in the pickup bay with a red brake lamp glow at its rear; the phone card still reads Ride requested. Same as option A for this interval.

Option B 2.0 to 2.8 s. Identical to option A: the car holds at the bay while a Texas locator card fades in, then at 2.6 s the film cuts to the cabin from behind the empty front seats, steering wheel at left, dash route screen and airplane sign through the windshield.

Option B 3.0 to 3.8 s. Same as option A: the empty-seat cabin view with the steering wheel marker turning clockwise with no hands, the airport sign sliding out of the windshield as the car moves, the dash route dot advancing and the Texas outline drawing at top right.
Option B 4.0 to 4.8 s. The cabin view holds unchanged, as in option A: wheel marker resting at right, windshield mostly blank with a sliver of the sign, empty seats, Texas locator top right.

Option B 5.0 to 5.8 s. Same as option A: the cabin holds to 5.2 s, then a curb close with a large tilted Ride requested phone in the left foreground and the white car at the bay behind it. Caption the airport included. Locator rings a county at 5.8 s.

Option B 6.0 to 6.8 s. Same as option A: the phone car icon reaches the pin and the screen changes from Ride requested to Arriving, At the curb, while the white car holds at the bay; the caption clears after 6.4 s.

Option B 7.0 to 7.8 s. Overhead framing of a flat paper map on an olive ground, with three small round roof-pod pins near center and a February calendar page at lower left. The map is nearly blank until 7.8 s, when a blue river stroke and thin lines begin drawing. The Texas locator stays at top right.

Option B 8.0 to 8.8 s. On the overhead map the blue river draws top to bottom, a second blue line appears at right and gray radial streets and a ring road draw in around the three roof-pod pins. The Texas locator fades away. The February page holds at lower left.

Option B 9.0 to 9.8 s. The overhead map holds, then at about 9.4 s the film cuts to the same tabletop map framing used in option A. The 60 square miles, Limited area tag swings onto the map, the February page slides in and lands at lower right, and a short dark outline stroke starts at upper left.

Option B 10.0 to 10.8 s. Same as option A: on the tabletop map the black outline traces clockwise from upper left across the top and down the right side toward the pins, while the February page shifts to the lower left. Still open at 10.8 s.
Option B 11.0 to 11.8 s. Same as option A: the outline closes into a shaded polygon around the three pins across the river under the 60 square miles tag, then holds.
Option B 12.0 to 12.8 s. Same as option A: the completed shaded service outline holds on the tabletop map, pins shifting slightly inside it, caption gone at 12.8 s.

Option B 13.0 to 13.8 s. After the last map frame, a cut to a straight-down view of a brown creek band between pale banks and round tree canopies. A white car seen from above, roof sensor disc visible, sits mid-channel with thin wake lines; it is nearly stationary across these samples. No rain marks visible. Disclosure reads Illustration. A different car, April 20th account.

Option B 14.0 to 14.8 s. The overhead creek view holds; the white car stays mid-channel with wake lines trailing left and a pale bow arc forming at its right end from 14.6 s. The car moves only slightly. No rain is drawn in these samples.

Option B 15.0 to 15.8 s. The overhead creek view holds to 15.2 s, then cuts at about 15.4 s to a water-level side view: the white roof-pod car half submerged in brown water with a bow wave at its front, a flat-topped tree on the bank behind and rain streaks. By 15.8 s it has shifted slightly right with its nose lifting. Dark seat shapes show in the windows.

Option B 16.0 to 16.8 s. Same treatment as option A for this interval: the half-submerged white car with a mud band keeps its place in frame while the bank trees slide left, a bow wave and spray at its front, rain streaks across the brown water.

Option B 17.0 to 17.8 s. The half-submerged creek car keeps moving right until the caption clears at 17.4 s, then the film cuts to the same flooded residential street wide used in option A: tan houses, a live oak, green street signs and a small white car in brown water, pale sidewalk in front.

Option B 18.0 to 18.8 s. Same as option A: the small white car rolls slowly right on the flooded street as the brown water climbs over its wheel arches, houses and a live oak behind, caption just beneath it.
Option B 19.0 to 19.8 s. Same as option A: the small white car stands stopped in floodwater above its wheel arches; tiny amber lamp glows appear at both ends from 19.6 s.

Option B 20.0 to 20.8 s. Same as option A: closer side view of the stopped white car in floodwater to the wheel arches, amber lamps at both ends glowing then dimming, empty seat shapes in the windows, houses and live oak softened behind.
Option B 21.0 to 21.8 s. Same as option A: the stopped white car holds in floodwater with amber lamps blinking at both ends and the water level steady; the frame drifts slightly.

Option B 22.0 to 22.8 s. After the stopped flood car, a cut to an overhead brown desk on an olive ground. A tilted cream card headed Federal recall record slides in from the right, its right edge cropped by the frame, with a blue pen at lower right. At 22.8 s field text begins typing: Reca, Sof.
Option B 23.0 to 23.8 s. On the overhead desk the record card settles and its rows type in: Recall type Software, then Potential units affected 3,791. The blue pen rests at lower right.

Option B 24.0 to 24.8 s. The finished record card holds on the overhead desk, then at about 24.6 s the framing becomes the same count-grid composition as option A: card near the top, a stamp handle edge at right, an empty car-outline grid below, and three white icons filling at 24.8 s.
Option B 25.0 to 25.8 s. Same as option A: the car-icon grid fills row by row below the record card while a blue-sleeved hand brings a wooden stamp in from the right toward the card header.

Option B 26.0 to 26.8 s. Same as option A: the stamp is pressed on the card header, the Nearly 3,800 vehicles counter tag swings in and settles above the full icon grid, and at 26.8 s the stamp lifts slightly to show an amber mark starting So.
Option B 27.0 to 27.8 s. Same as option A: the hand pulls the stamp away right, leaving an amber Software recall mark on the card, with the counter tag and full icon grid below.

Option B 28.0 to 28.8 s. After the finished record composition, a cut to a straight-down view of a two-lane road between grass verges with a small white car from above moving up the lane. At 28.6 s the caption box covers much of the car. At 28.8 s a translucent recall-sentence card fades in near the top. No water yet.

Option B 29.0 to 29.8 s. Overhead lane with the small white car near the lower middle while the lane dashes scroll past. A gray-blue water shape slides in from the top edge and grows. The quote card with the full recall sentence sits above. Caption just under the car.

Option B 30.0 to 30.8 s. In the overhead lane the gray-blue water shape grows down the upper lane, much of it behind the quote card, while the small white car holds near the lower middle. At 30.8 s two tiny red brake marks appear at the car's rear, a few pixels each at phone size.

Option B 31.0 to 31.8 s. Overhead: the small white car with tiny red brake marks holds below the gray-blue water shape, which fills the upper lane and is partly behind the quote card. A strip of open lane remains between car and water through 31.8 s.

Option B 32.0 to 32.8 s. Overhead, the white car creeps toward the water shape but has not entered it when the caption clears at 32.6 s. At 32.8 s the film cuts to the same close side view as option A: the large white roof-pod car on gray road with the quote card above, a thin pale wavy line at its tires.

Option B 33.0 to 33.8 s. Same as option A: close side view of the large white car; a pale water patch slides in from the right toward its front wheel but has not reached it by 33.8 s. Quote card above with no highlighted word.

Option B 34.0 to 34.8 s. Same as option A: the front wheel meets the standing water at 34.0 s and the water spreads under the front with ripples by 34.8 s; the word may in the quote card's first line gains an amber highlight at 34.2 s.

Option B 35.0 to 35.8 s. Same as option A: the large white car runs through pale standing water across its full length, diagonal wake lines trailing from its wheels and spray at the front tire, with the may highlight held on the quote card and the caption covering the lower wake.

Option B 36.0 to 36.8 s. Same as option A: the white car keeps rolling through the standing water with wake streaming from its wheels while the tree slides left; after the caption clears at 36.6 s the whole water patch and wake show under the car.

Option B 37.0 to 37.8 s. Cut to the record card lying flat on the overhead desk with its Software recall stamp. A Remedy row opens below the earlier fields and types The remedy is currently under development, completing and glowing warm peach by 37.6 s.
Option B 38.0 to 38.8 s. On the overhead card, a hand brings a pen in from the right at 38.2 s and rests its tip on the remedy row beside the words under development by 38.6 s.

Option B 39.0 to 39.8 s. Same as option A: the pen hand stays on the remedy row while a second blue-sleeved arm brings a wooden stamp from the lower right onto the lower remedy panel; two forearms from the right edge are on the card together.

Option B 40.0 to 40.8 s. Same as option A: the stamp presses the lower remedy panel, then lifts and slides right to reveal an amber Under development mark by 40.6 s, while the pen hand stays on the row.

Option B 41.0 to 41.8 s. The hands withdraw from the finished Under development card; at 41.6 s a cut to a straight-down parking lot with four white cars in bays, roof discs visible, an April calendar page at upper left. At 41.8 s a weather tag edge enters from the left.

Option B 42.0 to 42.8 s. In the overhead lot a Weather limits, tightened tag with a cloud and rain icon slides right along the top edge, overlapped by the April calendar page until about 42.6 s, and settles just right of it by 42.8 s. The four parked cars hold.
Option B 43.0 to 43.8 s. The overhead lot holds; the weather limits tag drifts slowly right along the top edge and tilts at 43.8 s. Cars and April page unchanged.
Option B 44.0 to 44.8 s. The overhead lot holds with only a slight rock of the weather limits tag; no check marks and no date change yet.

Option B 45.0 to 45.8 s. The overhead lot holds; the caption clears at 45.4 s, the framing pushes in slightly at 45.6 s and a small Vehicle maps card appears below the cars at lower right. The next caption appears at 45.8 s. No check marks yet; calendar shows only April.

Option B 46.0 to 46.8 s. Same sequence as option A from above: round check badges appear over the four parked cars one by one from left to right, the fourth drawing at 46.8 s. The calendar still shows only April.
Option B 47.0 to 47.8 s. All four cars carry check badges; a check draws on the Vehicle maps card with a tiny updated label. The calendar still reads only April through 47.8 s.
Option B 48.0 to 48.8 s. Same as option A: the checked lot holds, and at 48.8 s the calendar page flips to a large 20 under April, after all four cars already show checks.
Option B 49.0 to 49.8 s. Same as option A: the calendar settles on April 20 as the turned sheet lifts away; the checked cars, checked maps card and weather tag hold; caption clears at 49.8 s.

Option B 50.0 to 50.8 s. Same as option A: cut back to the airport curb with the white roof-pod car in the pickup bay beside the airplane sign and the phone card at upper left reading Arriving. Disclosure reads Illustration. A generic airport ride, not the flood cars.
Option B 51.0 to 51.8 s. Same as option A: the white car's rear side door opens from 51.2 s showing a dark interior and pale seat, and stays open at the airport bay.

Option B 52.0 to 52.8 s. Same as option A: the open-door car holds at the bay until the caption clears, then at 52.8 s a medium framing shows the curb and open-door car with a small phone at the curb and a small record card lying on the road in the foreground.

Option B 53.0 to 53.8 s. Same as option A: the open-door car holds at the bay while the small record card with its remedy row and Under development stamp floats on the road between car and caption, drifting slightly. Stamp text is not legible at phone size.
Option B 54.0 to 54.8 s. Same as option A: the record card grows and slides to the lower left until large and readable above the caption, its top edge reaching the open-door car's wheel line.
